reason: The pinned Git diff modifies HPresolve::dominatedColumns inside the MIP presolver. It monitors the cost and yield of predictive bound analysis and stops that analysis when domination checks are expensive and reductions are sparse. The PR reports no average speedup across its own 850-model sample, so it is a mechanism candidate for open_opportunity qualification, not an expert_reference performance claim.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: On MIPs with many columns where predictive bound analysis performs many domination checks but yields few reductions, stopping only that optional analysis can reduce presolve work and leave more of the fixed budget for solving. It can lose useful fixings on later columns.
causal_chain: The PR counts processed columns, predictive domination checks, and reductions. After each column it compares average checks and reductions against fixed internal thresholds, then gates later checkRow calls when neither implied bounds nor cliques require them. This changes which optional presolve scans run; any resulting solver benefit must be observed independently.
structural_trigger: A MIP whose dominated-columns reduction processes enough eligible columns to cross the predictive-check cost threshold while producing few fixings or bound changes. Include high-yield and low-column models as controls.
activation_probe: On public paired Base and PR builds, instrument dominatedColumns by processed column, predictive domination checks, fixings, bound changes, and skipped checkRow calls. Confirm the trigger requires the intended expensive low-yield path and that implied-bound or clique checks still execute.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze public diagnostic, hidden target, and control MIP families before hidden performance results. Stratify by column count, predictive-analysis check count and reduction yield observed on Base, sparsity, integrality mix, and Base proof difficulty. Keep generated variants of one model in a shared overlap group.
workload_exposure_plan: Build exact Base and Head source states with the common HiGHS driver and identical budgets, seeds, and solver settings. Establish activation on public diagnostic models. Use hidden target and control models for independently checked solution status, bounds, proof time, and regressions; retain all failures and missing runs.
mathematical_risk: The adaptive gate could skip a reduction that would become useful later or accidentally suppress mandatory implied-bound or clique reasoning. Counters may be stale when columns are deleted or fixed, and stopping a reduction can change later proof behavior or status claims.
independent_check_plan: Check all incumbents against the original MIP and verify objectives and valid bounds. For optimal and infeasible statuses use frozen trusted optima or an independent certificate or oracle, not incumbent feasibility alone. Compare small constructed models where predictive scans are costly, productive, or mandatory; preserve timeouts, crashes, and invalid outputs.
hidden_generalization_plan: Qualify only on a complete Base-only hidden baseline with stable, nondegenerate room in the predefined exact metric. The human PR's reported neutral aggregate is not grounds for rejection or a reference speedup. Judge fixed ID and shifted panels with valid solved coverage, proof time, timeout-bound progress, and per-family regressions; use separate qualification and final reporting evidence.
overlap_review: HiGHS #3035 caches repeated single-equation dual-fixing checks and #2917 changes single-equation handling. This PR gates predictive dominated-columns scans according to their observed cost and yield. It uses the same broad presolve phase but a distinct call path and mechanism; correlated MIP workloads should still be grouped in aggregate reporting.
resource_risk: Per-column accounting and branch checks add overhead to small or productive models; suppressing a useful later reduction can increase tree size, proof time, or memory.
